lit-crit-01-c3.text: Scott Bartling (2015). Beyond Language: Viktor Shklovsky, Estrangement, and the Search for Meaning in Art. PhD dissertation, Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures, Stanford University.
lit-crit-01-c3.quote: Russian Formalism was a school of criticism that formed around 1915-1916 and lasted until around 1930, after state suppression and the emigration of some of its leading members effectively put an end to its further development in the Soviet Union.
lit-crit-01-c3.claim: Earlier, and in parallel, came Russian Formalism, active roughly 1915-1930.

lit-crit-01-c3.text: Scott Bartling (2015). Beyond Language: Viktor Shklovsky, Estrangement, and the Search for Meaning in Art. PhD dissertation, Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures, Stanford University.
lit-crit-01-c3.quote: Its insights fared better in the West: Jakobson, who emigrated to Prague in 1920, was able to develop his version of Formalism with the members of the Prague Linguistic Circle under conditions of greater autonomy.
lit-crit-01-c3.claim: Many of its insights survived through Jakobson's later work in Prague and the United States, and they fed into structuralism.
